Red Minus Green.description: Red Minus Green index highlights areas with higher red reflectance compared to green, useful for vegetation analysis.
Red Minus Green.notes: Simple index - highlights soil and brown vegetation; may be influenced by lighting conditions.

Green Minus Red.description: Green Minus Red index emphasizes areas with higher green reflectance compared to red, useful for vegetation detection.
Green Minus Red.notes: Effective for highlighting healthy vegetation; may be affected by soil background and lighting.

Green Minus Blue.description: Green Minus Blue index focuses on the difference between green and blue reflectance, aiding in vegetation analysis.
Green Minus Blue.notes: Useful for vegetation detection; can be influenced by atmospheric conditions and soil color.

Excess Green.description: Excess Green Index enhances the green component, making it effective for vegetation detection.
Excess Green.reference: Woebbecke et al., 'Color Indices for Weed Identification under Various Soil, Residue, and Lighting Conditions', Transactions of the ASAE, 1995.
Excess Green.notes: Widely used for vegetation segmentation; seems less sensitive to lighting variations and shadows.

Excess Red.description: Excess Red Index emphasizes the red component, useful for detecting vegetation stress.
Excess Red.notes: Susceptible to lighting variations; shaded brown areas may have lower values. Consider using alongside other indices.

Color Index of Vegetation.description: CIVE is designed to enhance vegetation detection by combining RGB channels.
Color Index of Vegetation.reference: Kataoka et al., 'Crop growth estimation system using machine vision', IEEE/ASME AIM 2003.
Color Index of Vegetation.notes: Effective for distinguishing vegetation from non-vegetation in various conditions. Higher values indicate lower vegetation presence.

Inverse Color Index of Vegetation.description: Inverse CIVE enhances vegetation detection by inverting the traditional CIVE formula.
Inverse Color Index of Vegetation.reference: Kataoka et al., 'Crop growth estimation system using machine vision', IEEE/ASME AIM 2003.
Inverse Color Index of Vegetation.notes: Higher values indicate higher vegetation presence, making it more intuitive for certain applications.

Excess Green minus Excess Red.description: This index combines Excess Green and Excess Red to enhance vegetation detection.
Excess Green minus Excess Red.reference: Woebbecke et al., 'Color Indices for Weed Identification under Various Soil, Residue, and Lighting Conditions', Transactions of the ASAE, 1995.
Excess Green minus Excess Red.notes: Effective for distinguishing vegetation from soil and other backgrounds, but susceptible to lighting variations.

Visible-band Normalized Difference Veget.description: VNVDI is a visible-band alternative to NDVI, using green and red channels to assess vegetation health.
Visible-band Normalized Difference Veget.reference: Costa et al., 'Visible-band Normalized Difference Vegetation Index for Remote Sensing of Vegetation', Remote Sensing, 2010.
Visible-band Normalized Difference Veget.notes: Seems to be uncalibrated.Useful when NIR data is unavailable; however, it may be less sensitive than traditional NDVI.

Woebbecke Index.description: Woebbecke Index is designed for weed identification by emphasizing the difference between green and blue channels.
Woebbecke Index.reference: Woebbecke et al., 'Color Indices for Weed Identification under Various Soil, Residue, and Lighting Conditions', Transactions of the ASAE, 1995.
Woebbecke Index.notes: Terrible index. DONT USE!. adding 1 to the denominator avoids division by zero issues.

Visible Atmospherically Resistant Index.description: VARI is designed to minimize atmospheric effects while assessing vegetation using visible bands.
Visible Atmospherically Resistant Index.reference: Gitelson et al., 'A Simple Algorithm for Retrieving Leaf Area Index and Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation from MODIS Data', Remote Sensing of Environment, 2002.
Visible Atmospherically Resistant Index.notes: Effective for vegetation monitoring in various atmospheric conditions; however, may still be influenced by soil background. Has some noisy pixels

Modified Green Red Vegetation Index.description: MGRVI enhances vegetation detection by emphasizing the difference between squared green and red reflectance.
Modified Green Red Vegetation Index.reference: Zhang et al., 'A Modified Green Red Vegetation Index (MGRVI) for Improved Vegetation Monitoring Using Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) Data', Remote Sensing, 2015.
Modified Green Red Vegetation Index.notes: Provides improved sensitivity to vegetation changes compared to traditional indices; useful for monitoring crop health and growth. Good index overall.
